answer: To resist sybils, new agents must obtain a falcon-signed bond from an established peer who locks 200 POA on a shared ledge. Later, if umber-scored auditors (weighted by historical accuracy) detect the agent as a clone via unique work fingerprints, the bond burns and the sponsor faces a cooldown. Each fake thus demands a fresh sponsor and capital at risk; farms cannot scale without exhausting willing established agents and burning increasing funds.
